rules.name: AIT to application CI (VAMP)
USEM AIT to business application
USEM Manual ingestion hostname match
USEM Serial Number Class Match
rules.description: Serial number resolved strictly inside the CI class implied by the scanned OS. Junk serials filtered; unique owner required.

rules.name: USEM Serial Number Hardware Match
rules.description: Serial number resolved across the cmdb_ci_hardware subtree when the OS gives no usable class. Junk serials filtered; unique owner required.

rules.name: USEM Cisco IP Phone MAC
rules.description: Cisco Unified CM phones report SEP<MAC> as their DNS label. Derives the MAC and matches strictly within cmdb_ci_ip_phone (adapter, mac_address, or SEP device name).

rules.name: USEM FQDN Class Match
rules.description: Exact FQDN inside the OS-implied class; duplicate FQDNs resolve only when the scanned IP corroborates a single candidate.

rules.name: USEM FQDN Hardware Match
rules.description: Exact FQDN across the cmdb_ci_hardware subtree; duplicate FQDNs resolve only when the scanned IP corroborates a single candidate.

rules.name: USEM Hostname Domain Class Match
rules.description: Combination match inside the OS-implied class: CI name = hostname AND fqdn/dns_domain confirms the domain. Scanned IP breaks ties.

rules.name: USEM Hostname Domain Hardware Match
rules.description: Combination match (name + domain evidence) across the cmdb_ci_hardware subtree for generically classed CIs. Scanned IP breaks ties.

rules.name: USEM Layered DNS Match
rules.description: Resolves the scanned DNS name through the layered CMDB model (DNS name -> IP address -> adapter -> owning CI) so aliases land on the device that answers on that name.

rules.name: USEM Hostname Class Match
rules.description: Unique short hostname inside the OS-implied class, for CIs without FQDN/domain data.

rules.name: USEM Hostname Hardware Match
rules.description: Unique short hostname across cmdb_ci_hardware; rejects owners whose class contradicts the scanned OS.

rules.name: USEM FQDN Name Hardware Match
rules.description: CI named with the full FQDN string, hardware subtree only; unique owner required.

rules.name: USEM IP Class Match
rules.description: Last-resort IP matching, stage 1: address must belong to exactly one CI of the OS-implied class.

rules.name: USEM IP Hardware Match
rules.description: Last-resort IP matching, stage 2: unique owner across cmdb_ci_hardware; load-balancer VIPs and OS-contradicting owners rejected.

rules.name: USEM IP Adapter Match
rules.description: Last-resort IP matching, stage 3: address resolved through the network adapter to a single owning CI; VIPs rejected.

rules.name: USEM IP Layered Match
rules.description: Last-resort IP matching, stage 4: address resolved through the layered IP model (IP record -> adapter -> owning CI); VIPs rejected.

rules.name: USEM FQDN Name Broad Match
rules.description: The single deliberately-late broad fallback: CI named with the full FQDN anywhere outside the ignored classes; unique owner required.

Note: If you already have an active IP lookup rule which checks "cmdb_ci", then no need to activate this rule.

oob.name: Mac Address
oob.script: (function process(rule, sourceValue, sourcePayload) { /********************************* * CI Lookup Rule Script * * Available variables: * - sourceValue: The value of the source field from incoming data that is used for lookup * - rule: Reference to the lookup rule that is being evaluated * - sourcePayload: All the fields from incoming data that can be used for matching CI * * Return either: * - the sysid of the CI that was matched by the rule * - null if there were no CI records that matched **********************************/ return null; })(rule, sourceValue, sourcePayload);

oob.name: FQDN
oob.script: // _queryMatch function checks if the query returns 0, 1 or more than 1 CI. // it returns: // null: if no CI found // ci record: if a unique CI was found // the first CI record found: if more than 1 CI was found and log a duplicate error message // To avoid specific CI classes ,add the class names, comma separated, to the property sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass (function process(rule, sourceValue, sourcePayload) { var sourceField = {}; var ignore = global.SecProperty.getProperty("sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass", ""); sourceField[rule.source_field] = sourceValue; gs.warn("......identify lookup rule " + sourceValue + " ignore:" +ignore + ": " + JSON.stringify(rule)); var cmdbci = new GlideRecord("cmdb_ci"); cmdbci.addQuery("fqdn", "IN", sourceValue); if (!gs.nil(ignore)) cmdbci.addQuery('sys_class_name','NOT IN', ignore); cmdbci.query(); while(cmdbci.next()){ gs.warn("......identify lookup rule cmdbci.name " + cmdbci.name); } cmdbci = new GlideRecord("cmdb_ci"); cmdbci.addQuery("fqdn", "IN", sourceValue); if (!gs.nil(ignore)) cmdbci.addQuery('sys_class_name','NOT IN', ignore); cmdbci.query(); cmdbci = _queryMatch(cmdbci, rule, sourceField); gs.warn("......identify lookup rule cmdbci.getUniqueValue " + cmdbci.getUniqueValue()); if (cmdbci) return cmdbci.getUniqueValue(); return null; })(rule, sourceValue, sourcePayload);
